title: Request Path Governance: Schema + Promotion Playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose and scope

This doc captures a contract-first approach for authoring request-governance rules (what we previously referred to as routing rules) and a pragmatic promotion/playbook for validating and rolling them out across regions and deployment types (hosted/dedicated/private). The intent is to be prescriptive enough for SRE/Platform engineers to validate safety properties and lightweight enough for product engineers to author.

Design principles (short)
- Contract-first: every rule must conform to a machine-checked JSON Schema before it is accepted by the control plane.
- Intentional defaults: safe conservative defaults to avoid accidental global traffic shifts.
- Observable gating: each promotion step requires specific telemetry artifacts (latency, error rates, cost delta, sample response checks).
- Region-awareness: rules can include explicit per-region overrides; cross-region fallbacks must be explicit.
- Rollouts as state machines: we define a finite set of rollout phases and transitions with clear automated and manual gates.

High-level schema summary (human readable)
- id: unique rule id (uuid or dashed token)
- description: free-text intent
- match: set of predicates (header, path prefix, model type, client id, token bucket)
- actions: prioritized list: route -> variant, weight, redirect, transform
- constraints: latency_slo_ms, max_cost_delta_pct, allowed_regions, allowed_tiers
- safety: kill-switch boolean, emergency-fallback target, sample-log: true/false
- rollout: policy object (phases array) describing initial canary, ramp, steady, cooldown, and abort behavior

Example JSON Schema (simplified, for validator)
{
  "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#",
  "title": "request-governance-rule",
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["id","match","actions","rollout"],
  "properties": {
    "id": {"type":"string"},
    "description": {"type":"string"},
    "match": {
      "type":"object",
      "properties": {
        "path_prefix": {"type":"string"},
        "headers": {"type":"object","additionalProperties":{"type":"string"}},
        "client_id": {"type":"string"},
        "model_family": {"type":"string"}
      },
      "additionalProperties": false
    },
    "actions": {
      "type":"array",
      "minItems": 1,
      "items": {
        "type":"object",
        "required":["type"],
        "properties":{
          "type":{"enum":["route","redirect","reject","transform"]},
          "target":{"type":"string"},
          "weight":{"type":"number","minimum":0,"maximum":1},
          "metadata":{"type":"object"}
        }
      }
    },
    "constraints":{
      "type":"object",
      "properties":{
        "latency_slo_ms":{"type":"number"},
        "max_cost_delta_pct":{"type":"number"},
        "allowed_regions":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}}
      }
    },
    "safety":{
      "type":"object",
      "properties":{
        "kill_switch":{"type":"boolean"},
        "emergency_fallback":{"type":"string"},
        "sample_log":{"type":"boolean"}       
      }
    },
    "rollout":{
      "type":"object",
      "required":["phases"],
      "properties":{
        "phases":{
          "type":"array",
          "items":{
            "type":"object",
            "required":["name","duration_seconds"],
            "properties":{
              "name":{"type":"string"},
              "duration_seconds":{"type":"number"},
              "target_percentage":{"type":"number","minimum":0,"maximum":100},
              "checks":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}}
            }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  },
  "additionalProperties": false
}

Authoring ergonomics and recommended fields
- Keep match predicate narrow for canaries: prefer explicit client_id or path_prefix rather than broad header rules.
- Add a short intent sentence in description: who will be impacted and why this change exists.
- Use constraints.latency_slo_ms to surface SLO-based gating. If unset, default to platform global SLO.
- Set safety.kill_switch: false by default in authoring, but ensure the control plane injects an env-level override that operators can flip.

Validation and pre-flight checks (automated)
1) Schema validation: reject if JSON Schema fails.
2) Static verification: ensure action targets exist in the model catalog and the region constraints are compatible with target capacity. (lookup via model-registry API)
3) Traffic overlap analysis: compute intersection with active rules using match predicate SAT heuristics. Flag shadow overlaps > 1% of traffic to same client_id.
4) Cost delta estimate: simulate expected token rate and charge per-token for candidate targets vs baseline. Reject if cost delta > constraints.max_cost_delta_pct (if specified) or hard limit at 50%.
5) Canary safety check: authoring flow enforces that initial canary <= 1% traffic or explicit client_id whitelists.
6) Offline smoke tests: run a tiny synthetic sample through the exact rule in a local sandbox to ensure no JSONPath/transform exceptions.

Promotion/playbook (phased rollout)
We treat rollouts as a 5-stage state machine with automated checks at each transition. Each phase is time-bounded and optionally requires manual approval to proceed if checks do not pass automatically.
- phase: init_canary
  - goal: verify basic correctness and no immediate errors against a small scoped subset of traffic (client-id or path-prefix).
  - default target_percentage: 0.5% or explicit client whitelist.
  - mandatory checks: functional_success_rate >= 99%, no error spike > 2x baseline, no schema/transform exceptions.
  - telemetry windows: 5m, 30m.
- phase: regional_ramp
  - goal: expand across allowed_regions with conservative weight per region.
  - default progression: 0.5% -> 5% over 2h per region.
  - mandatory checks: latency_p50/p95 within constraints, cost_delta trending below threshold, per-region error rates stable.
- phase: load_ramp
  - goal: increase to target_percentage (e.g., 25%) while watching load-specific regressions (CPU, GPU queue depth).
  - mandatory checks: infra backpressure metrics under configured quanta, stability for 1h.
- phase: steady_state
  - goal: run for an observation window (default 24h) and gather quality regressions from eval harness (prompt set).
  - mandatory checks: no regression alerts from Redwood Optimize baseline; user-facing error budgets intact.
- phase: promote_full / abort
  - goal: either promote to full rule (100% or replacing legacy routes) or abort/rollback to emergency_fallback.
  - mandatory checks: product and SRE sign-off for non-automated promotions.

Automation and gating heuristics
- Automated gates evaluate: error rate delta, latency percentile delta, cost delta, model output quality delta (via golden prompts), and infra signals (GPU queue length). Each check returns pass/warn/fail.
- Composite gate rule: fail if any check returns fail; warn if more than 2 warn signals. Manual intervention required on warn.
- If an automated gate fails during a ramp, transition to abort state and route traffic to emergency_fallback immediately (circuit-breaker).
- Soft cooldown: when a failed gate recovers within a short window (configurable 10m), we can optionally resume ramp at previous safe percentage with operator opt-in.

Multi-region specifics
- Explicit region mapping required for any rule touching multi-region targets. Implicit global routing is disallowed for new rules.
- Latency SLOs and cost deltas evaluated on a per-region basis. A rule may be promoted in region A while remaining in init_canary in region B.
- Staggered promotions recommended: prefer sequential regional ramps ordered by traffic volume and customer criticality.
- Cross-region failover must list allowed_fallback_regions and a bandwidth cap to avoid cost explosions.

Rollback criteria and recovery
- Immediate rollback triggers: >=5x error spike or >=200ms p95 latency regression sustained for 5m, or infrastructure OOM/queue-saturation alarms.
- Partial rollback: reduce percentage back to last-known-good phase at operator discretion.
- Post-rollback forensics: automated snapshot of request/response samples (redacted), infra metrics, and the exact rule JSON saved to incremental audit log.

Testing playbook (pre-authoring, pre-promotion, post-promotion)
- pre-authoring: review existing active rules that might overlap; pick client ids for canary.
- pre-promotion: run schema check, static verification, cost estimate, dry-run in sandbox with 1000 synthetic requests, and run a golden prompt eval set (10 prompts).
- post-promotion: after each phase, run full golden prompt eval and a 24h drift check; persist evaluation results to the rule audit entry.

Operational runbook snippets
- Emergency disable (operator CLI): redwoodctl rules disable <rule-id> --reason "emergency"
- Force promote to region (manual): redwoodctl rules promote <rule-id> --region us-west-2 --to-phase load_ramp --force
- Inspect active overlaps: redwoodctl rules overlap <rule-id> --granularity client_id
- Fetch audit: redwoodctl rules audit <rule-id> --since 2026-03-01

Example authoring YAML (simple canary)
---
id: rp-2026-0310-mlqa
description: "Canary: use llama-2-small-quant for /api/v1/qa requests from test-client"
match:
  path_prefix: "/api/v1/qa"
  client_id: "internal-test-suite"
actions:
  - type: route
    target: "llama-2-small-quant-v1"
    weight: 1.0
constraints:
  latency_slo_ms: 150
  max_cost_delta_pct: 10
  allowed_regions: ["us-west-2"]
safety:
  kill_switch: true
  emergency_fallback: "default-llama-2"
rollout:
  phases:
    - name: init_canary
      duration_seconds: 3600
      target_percentage: 0.5
      checks: ["functional_success_rate","no_transform_exceptions"]
    - name: regional_ramp
      duration_seconds: 7200
      target_percentage: 5
      checks: ["p95_latency","error_rate"]

Notes on examples and ownership
- Keep example rule ids traceable to a ticket (e.g., rp-YYYYMMDD-<short>).
- Every accepted rule must be associated with an oncall owner field in the control plane (currently we inherit from the GitHub PR author). We should make this explicit in metadata in the next iteration.

Open questions / follow-ups
- How do we incorporate model-level A/B quality checks into the automated gates without leaking PII? (short term: use synthetic golden prompts, redact outputs)
- Should we support percentage-based region overrides (e.g., 2% us-east-1, 8% eu-west-1) or insist on per-region discrete ramps? Proposal: allow percentages but require an explicit region distribution block.
- Audit retention: what retention policy for saved sample responses is compliant with enterprise customers? (security to advise on redact pattern)

Appendix: quick checklist for reviewers (pre-merge)
- [ ] JSON Schema passes locally
- [ ] model targets exist + capacity reservation check passed
- [ ] cost delta estimate recorded
- [ ] canary traffic scoping verified (client ids or path_prefix)
- [ ] kill_switch set & emergency_fallback valid
- [ ] phased rollout defined with checks and durations
- [ ] at least one collaborator reviewed

End of doc.
